audits.area: Recruit board and slots (ideation/wave1, /home/alex/code/Bramble-ideation-balance): slot labels, ring/count badges, grooves and diagonals, row labels, slot banners, empty-slot labels, slot effect marks, lane projection/overlay

items.element: Name strip above/below every tile ("F1 Annis ×2", "B2 Redbreast")
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/board_view.gd _place_label (203), strips built in _init, LABEL_H 44 + LABEL_GAP 6 added per row in _row_height; fit_name (251)
items.shows: Slot code, unit name (often cut to the last word or blank), and the Ring count
items.why: An experienced player knows units by their art. Battlegrounds shows no minion names on the board. The name is one tap away in the reader. Card text never uses slot codes (the wording guide uses beside, next to, across), so F1/B2 is extra vocabulary on every tile. The strips cost 100 of the 1080 canvas px. In reader mode (reel-mistress screenshot) the strip shows "+3/+3 · 2" in place of the name.
items.replacement: Nothing on the board. The name goes to the reader. The Ring count moves onto the fairy ring (see the Ring count item). Spend the 100 px on bigger pockets (raise BOARD_POCKET/READING_POCKET) so the stat beads read better on phones.

items.element: Slot-code chips on tiles and marked empty slots (F1…B3 on the bottom edge in combat and scout; the chip on an empty Ring or Nest slot)
items.where: Combat, scout and recruit. src/ui/widgets/board_view.gd _slot_chip (85); the chip_on branch of _place_label (203)
items.shows: Which labelled slot a tile stands in
items.why: Position shows in the brick itself, and "across" is the same spot on the mirrored brick. Attack order (F1→F4, then B1→B3) is taught on the how-to-play page "Who attacks when". A player who knows the game never reads these.
items.replacement: None on the board. Tutorial diagrams keep the labels.

items.element: Empty-pocket text: big "F3" plus the note "before B2 & B3" / "behind F3 & F4" (recruit); big "B2" plus "EMPTY" (scout and combat)
items.where: Recruit, scout and combat. src/ui/widgets/slot_view.gd _init (35-49), note() (60), _refresh_labels (70); with_notes set by board_view.configure
items.shows: The slot's name, that it is empty, and which slots it sits between
items.why: This is the chess-knight sign: it teaches the brick geometry on every empty slot in every game. An empty carved pocket already shows that it is empty, and the half-slot offset shows which two front slots a back slot sits between. The how-to-play page "Your board is a brick wall" already teaches this.
items.replacement: Keep only the bare carved pocket with its dashed edge. The geometry stays on the tutorial page "Your board is a brick wall".

items.element: Row tags FRONT / BACK (and SHOP), burned vertical words
items.shows: Which row is front and which is back
items.why: Your front row is always the top row, toward the shop and the enemy. That gets learned in one game and is taught on the page "The front row takes the hits". The tags take the left gutter and push the hero plaque out.
items.replacement: None. The board and hero plaque can move left into the gutter.

items.element: Dotted grooves (the diagonals) from each back pocket to the two front pockets ahead of it, lit gold when both ends are occupied
items.where: Recruit, scout and combat. src/ui/widgets/board_view.gd _draw_grooves (330), called from _draw
items.shows: The in-front-of/behind links and, lit, which links of the touching zigzag are unbroken
items.why: The owner named these. The brick offset already shows which front slots each back slot sits between. A lit groove only means both slots hold units, which the tiles already show.
items.replacement: No lines at rest. When an effect that uses a relation fires (on play, End of Turn or Start of Combat), a spark leaves the source tile's centre and travels straight to each affected tile (0.25 s, ease-out), then that tile's stat bead bumps (scale 1.15, 0.15 s) with a "+X" pop. For Touching effects the spark hops tile to tile along the run in zigzag order, 0.08 s per hop, and stops where a gap breaks the run. Nothing stays on the board afterwards.

items.element: Relation highlight: gilt fill and outline on the slots a unit's text reaches, shown on select, during drag and after placing; plus the reader line "Highlighted: B1 and B2."
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/board_view.gd show_relations (442); src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd 506 (select), 773 (drag), 901 (after placing); src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd geometry_note (594)
items.shows: Which slots "behind / in front / next to / beside" covers from this slot
items.why: The highlight stays on after a placement and on plain selection, so it is a static marker of where things are. The geometry is a rule an experienced player knows. The one moment it helps a decision is while choosing a drop slot.
items.replacement: Only while dragging a unit whose text reaches other slots, over a candidate pocket: the units it would reach lean 6 px toward that pocket and back (0.15 s ease-in-out), replaying when the hovered pocket changes. No highlight on tap-select or after the drop: the spark from the grooves item shows the effect when it fires. Cut the "Highlighted:" reader line.

items.element: Permanent "Pass end" banner and moss arrow on the last unit in the zigzag
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/slot_marks.gd _place (183-193), _pass_landing (196), _draw (255-262); src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd slot_marks (278-283) sets pass_end whenever the board has any unit
items.shows: Which unit a Pass would land on
items.why: It shows even when no unit on the board has Pass (lobby and natural-birds screenshots), and it covers the art of the end unit. The recipient follows from the rule (the last occupied slot in F1-B1-F2-B2-F3-B3-F4) plus the visible board.
items.replacement: No permanent mark. The Pass itself animates at End of Turn (next item). Rulebook 12.1.6 requires "the permanent Pass mark", so that line must be edited and the deviation logged in docs/ideation/DECISIONS.md.

items.element: "Pass lands" preview arrow while selecting, hovering or dragging a Pass source, and the hover line "Pass order: F1-B1-F2-B2-F3-B3-F4. Lands at End of Turn."
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/slot_marks.gd pass_slot setter and _draw; src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd 497, 564-566, 771; src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd geometry_note (596-604)
items.shows: The actual recipient, and the zigzag order as text
items.why: This is a targeting arrow plus a rules reminder. The order is taught on the page "Follow the zigzag" and in the Pass reminder slip.
items.replacement: At End of Turn each Pass resolves as a glowing seed. It leaves the source and hops pocket to pocket along F1→B1→F2→B2→F3→B3→F4, skipping empty pockets, 0.07 s per hop. It lands on the recipient with a "+X" pop and a 0.2 s stat bump. A combat Pass flies straight to its recipient in 0.3 s. The reader of a Pass unit gets one line, "Passes to: <name>" or "No one to pass to". The zigzag sentence goes to the Pass reminder slip.

items.element: Ring count/stat badge: "×2" in the name strip, "+3/+3 · 2" in reader-mode strips, and floating "+2/+2" / "+4/+4" badges on tiles (scout and lobby screenshots)
items.where: Recruit and scout. src/ui/widgets/slot_marks.gd _ring_words (136), _place (155-180), header_width (121); data from src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd _ring_marks (286)
items.shows: Ring stats on the slot, and how many Rings
items.why: The unit's stat beads already include the Ring bonus, so the +X/+X repeats them. The count is state the player can't see elsewhere: Rings stay on the slot when the unit moves, Reel-Mistress moves them, and Ring size multiplies by the count. That makes it a real build investment on your own board.
items.replacement: On your own board only, a single digit on one toadstool at the ring's bottom-right corner (cream disc, ink digit, UiTheme.MIN_FONT 31), shown only when the count is 2 or more. A lone Ring is just the dots. Scout and enemy boards show dots only, with the count in the reader. Animation when a Ring is added: toadstools sprout clockwise round the pocket (0.3 s) and the digit ticks up. When one moves, they hop to the new pocket (0.3 s).

items.element: Fairy-ring dots round the pocket (26 dots, 8 px radius)
items.shows: This slot carries one or more Rings
items.why: It is a state visual like Battlegrounds' Taunt frame. It matters for moving and placing units and can't be inferred. At 8 px it reads as a heavy bead chain that competes with the grooves and the tile edge.
items.replacement: Same ring, dots reduced to about 5 px outer radius with a thin ink rim, so it reads as a frame. The count digit sits on it (see the Ring count item).

items.element: Rainbow band (painted slot), a coloured bar at the pocket's foot
items.shows: That the slot is painted, in the slot's own colour
items.why: Painted lasts until the unit moves or leaves, so it can't be inferred later. It is already small and wordless.
items.replacement: No change at rest. When a unit paints the slot on play, the colour wipes left to right across the band (0.3 s).

items.element: Horseshoe icon (the one-fight slot spell)
items.shows: This slot has the one-fight Horseshoe bonus
items.why: It is hidden slot state, a small icon with no words, and it marks the one-fight spell apart from a permanent Ring.
items.replacement: No change.

items.element: Empty Nest: egg art in 22 woven twigs, 64 px egg stat beads, and the label "Egg · home in 2"
items.shows: The Egg that fights in this slot, its stats, and the turns until the Bird comes home
items.why: The Egg is a real fighter, so keep its art and stats as you would a unit's. The countdown is hidden state. The sentence is a reminder, and the beads are drawn bigger than unit beads.
items.replacement: Egg-in-nest art filling the pocket like a tile. Stat beads at the normal board-tile bead size. The countdown as a lone digit on a small feather badge in the pocket's top-right (MIN_FONT). The sentence stays in the reader (RecruitHeld.egg_card already says "X comes home in N turns"). Animation: at End of Turn the digit flips down. On homecoming the Bird swoops in from the top edge to its slot (0.6 s) and the egg cracks.

items.element: "On Nest 1" banner on a unit standing on a Nest (placed between the rows)
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/slot_marks.gd _place_nest_label (the "On " prefix and its placement below front tiles / above back tiles)
items.shows: This slot is a Nest under a unit, and the turns until its Bird returns
items.why: It is needed: the returning Bird needs room, and the Egg fights there if the unit leaves. It isn't visible any other way. But the words, and a banner straddling both rows, are too much.
items.replacement: A thin twig rim round the pocket edge (inside the fairy ring if both are present), plus the same feather-badge countdown digit. No words. The unit's reader adds "On Mrs Jay's Nest: home in 1 turn."

items.element: Scout lane forecast: dashed hunter lines from your Quarry units to their targets, Mire reed lines, gold paws on enemy tiles, mud patches labelled "MIRE" / "F2 MIRE", and the pack bracket
items.where: Recruit, scouting. src/ui/widgets/lane_overlay.gd _draw (35-80), _draw_patch (95-117); src/ui/lane_projection.gd forecast; src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd 257; recruit_layout.gd 182
items.shows: A forecast of who your Quarry hunters and their Mire units will bind
items.why: These are static images of relations the rules already give: Quarry and Mire both act on "the enemy across". They forecast against the opponent's last board, which is not the board you will face. In the scout screenshot the lines cross both boards and cover the art.
items.replacement: Nothing in scout. The fight shows it as it happens (next item).

items.element: Combat lane overlay: the same hunter lines, paws on quarries, and mud patches with the word MIRE
items.shows: Live quarry marks and Mire patches during the fight
items.why: A quarry and a patch are real fight state: they can be lost or broken, and units relocate. A small mark on the target earns its place. The lines between tiles are relation pictures.
items.replacement: At Start of Combat each hunter's paw print stamps in two hops from the hunter to its quarry (0.35 s), leaving only a 22 px paw at the quarry's top-right. A Mire unit's mud splashes across to the enemy slot (0.3 s), leaving a thin mud strip with reeds at that pocket's foot and no word. Lines are never drawn. When a quarry is lost or a patch breaks, its paw or mud fades out (0.2 s). The combat-UI reviewer may cover the same widget.

items.element: Hex slip in fights ("Hex -3 / -50%")
items.shows: The running Hex total on a slot, whoever stands there
items.why: It is real slot state with no other display. The word "Hex" is a reminder.
items.replacement: A purple sigil disc reading "-3" (or "-50%") at the pocket foot. On application the sigil drops from the caster onto the slot (0.3 s) and the number ticks.

items.element: "Board 7/7" chip under the hand
items.shows: Units on the board out of 7
items.why: All seven pockets are always drawn, so the count is visible at a glance.
items.replacement: None. Dropping onto a full board already gets refused.

items.element: Legal-target pocket highlight during drag, aim or tap-to-move
items.shows: Where the held card can go right now
items.why: It is feedback during an action, not a standing image. Phone tap-to-move needs visible targets, and it clears when the action ends.
items.replacement: No change.

items.element: Reader slot note ("F1: Ring +3/+3 · 2, Rainbow band.") and the Nest sentence
items.where: Card reader. src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd slot_note (391), with_slot_note (358); recruit_held.gd nest_note (181)
items.shows: Full slot state for the selected unit
items.why: This is already the right place, one tap away. It becomes where the cut strip, the Ring stats and the nest words live.
items.replacement: Keep it in the reader without slot codes: "This slot: 2 Rings (+3/+3), painted." and "On Mrs Jay's Nest: home in 1 turn."

items.element: "Ring size 1.25" chip above the shop
items.shows: The player-wide multiplier for each Ring
items.why: Ringed units' stats already include it. The number only matters when choosing a Ring card or Fairy, and that card's reader can show it live. It borders the header area.
items.replacement: The Ring reminder slip, and the reader of any Ring spell, Fairy or ringed slot, shows "Your Ring size: +1.25/+1.25."

items.element: Pocket shape: carved pocket with a dashed edge when empty, a solid ink edge when filled, shaded top lip, and the oak brick tray
items.where: Recruit, scout and combat. src/ui/widgets/slot_view.gd _draw (94); board_view.gd _draw
items.shows: The 4-3 brick, and which slots are open
items.why: This is the horse on the chessboard: the board itself, with no words.
items.replacement: No change, apart from the bigger pockets the space from the cut name strips allows.

audits.notes:
1. Text that still uses slot codes. The cuts take F1-B3 off the board. Several pieces of text still use the codes: the Behind and Touching reminders in src/ui/keyword_rules.gd ("B1 behind F1 and F2"), the zigzag line, the Birds-away tray ("· F3") and the how-to-play pages "Who attacks when" and "Follow the zigzag". Either the tutorial diagrams show the labels so the reminders still make sense, or the reminders are reworded ("the two front slots it sits between", "the zigzag between rows").

2. Docs and rules to update in the same step, with the reasons logged in docs/ideation/DECISIONS.md:
   - Rulebook 12.1.6 requires "the permanent Pass mark".
   - Wording guide, "Let the interface carry it": it counts "selecting a unit lights the slots its text reaches" as an existing cue.
   - The how-to-play already has "Your board is a brick wall" and "Follow the zigzag", so moving the teaching there needs no new pages. Those pages should use the same spark and Pass-seed animations as their teaching visuals.

3. Nest countdown appears twice: on the nest ("Egg · home in 2") and in the Birds-away tray ("home in 2 turns · F3"). Pick one on-board home, the feather-badge digit, and let the tray become reader content. The tray belongs to another area.

4. Combat overlaps. The combat lane overlay, Hex slip and slot chips are drawn by my area's widgets but appear on the combat screen, so the combat reviewer may judge them too. Lines in fights should go everywhere, consistent with the owner's "targeting arrows" remark.

5. Space returned. The name strips are 2 × (44 + 6) = 100 of 1080 canvas px. The row tags and grooves also take room. Spend it on larger pockets so tile stat beads read better on phone, not on new widgets.

6. One verified bug. The "Pass end" mark shows whenever the board has any unit, even with no Pass unit on it (recruit_view.gd slot_marks 278-283 doesn't check for a Pass source).

7. Not done. I did not run Godot. Judgements come from the code on ideation/wave1 and the listed screenshots: the redbreast-label overview, away-tray PC, the Reel-Mistress reader, wording2 combat_mid, round4-geometry, natural-birds, recruit_frozen, and strong-field scout and lobby.

audits.area: Units and cards everywhere: shop, board, hand and combat tiles, on-tile overlays (chips, counters, statuses, golden, frost, nest, ring, pass, hex, quarry), and the one-tap card reader

items.element: Trigger/ability text chip on tiles (End of Turn, Start of Combat, Homecoming, Take reward, On play, When hit, Gives Pass, Ring dance, Ability...)
items.where: Board tiles in recruit, combat and scout; shop and hand tiles on phone. card_view.gd:600-657 (_refresh_chip), 174-229 (chip_text/_rules_chip/_rules_tag), RULE_TAGS 51-101
items.shows: When a card's ability fires, or a short paraphrase of what it does
items.why: An experienced player knows each card's ability from its portrait. On a 189-px board tile on phone, the two-line chip covers about 45% of the art. All it adds on the board is 'this unit will do something', and the player should see that happen, not read it.
items.replacement: Static part: one 44-px glyph at the bottom centre between the stat beads, where Battlegrounds puts its skull and lightning bolt. Use the existing Icons 'spark' for any trigger and 'bones' for When this dies. On play gets no glyph. Animation in every phase, when the ability fires: (1) the glyph scales 1.0 to 1.6 to 1.0 over 0.25 s with a warm flash; (2) the tile hops 12 px and back in 0.18 s; (3) one 16-px gold mote per affected unit flies from source to target on a shallow arc in 0.3 s, staggered 0.05 s; (4) the target's changed bead pops 1.0 to 1.3 to 1.0 over 0.2 s while its number ticks to the new value. The recruit phase gets this too. On play and After you cast fire right after the action. After End turn is pressed, End of Turn units fire one by one in zigzag order, 0.35 s each, before the fight screen; a tap skips. Reduce motion: glyph flash and bead pop only. Delete RULE_TAGS, TAG_KEYWORDS and the 'Ability' fallback.

items.element: Printed keywords written on the chip (Quarry, Mire, Snap, Pack, Cleave, Shy, Peck 2, Bristle 2, Belly 1, Ring +1/+1, Rainbow, 'Gives Nightshade')
items.where: Same chip. card_view.gd:190-215 (keyword-first chip), 606-614 ('Gives' trim), 633 (Nightshade colour)
items.shows: The card's main keyword
items.why: A printed keyword is part of the card's identity, so an experienced player already knows it (the knight). It shows when it happens. Keywords that can be granted during play are statuses and get their own visuals (status item).
items.replacement: Nothing static. The fight shows each keyword when it acts. Cleave: the lunge ends in a sideways sweep, and both units beside the target shake and show their damage burst together. Peck N: N jabs of 0.12 s each, one burst per jab. Pack: joiners lunge from their own slots 0.05 s after the attacker. Quarry and Snap: the attacker skips the usual target and lunges diagonally at its own. Shy: when it leaves, it slides off the board edge over 0.4 s and a coin drops onto the gold plaque's Next figure. Ring, Hex and Belly carry their own slot or counter visuals (items below). The reader keeps every keyword link.

items.element: Rules text on shop unit tiles (always on desktop, short texts on phone)
items.shows: The card's full rules
items.why: This is the sign on the knight: needed once per card, then passed over for hundreds of games. It also shrinks the portrait to ART_MIN 40 px. Battlegrounds' tavern shows minions with no text and the full card on hover.
items.replacement: Shop units use the board tile: a portrait filling the tile, the stat beads and the glyph. Full text in the reader on hover (PC) or tap (phone), as now.

items.element: Unit name on shop tiles
items.shows: Which card it is
items.why: Players recognise units by portrait, and the name takes one or two lines at 34 px. Catch: on this branch, 50 of 157 unit files have no portrait of their own and fall back to a shared tribe portrait (ui_theme.gd:210-228; several Hedgerow mice share one face in evidence/ui/recruit_frozen). For those units, the name is the only identifier.
items.replacement: Drop the name once every unit has its own portrait, which Done means 5 already requires. Until then, show one line on fallback-portrait units only: the short name (BoardView.fit_name's last-word rule) at the 31 minimum, under the art.

items.element: Tribe word under shop tiles (Hedgerow, Birds, Fairies, Neutral)
items.shows: The card's tribe
items.why: A card's tribe never changes and an experienced player knows it. The reader's type line already shows it in capitals.
items.replacement: The reader type line only.

items.element: Spell and item tiles: rules text, name, and the 'Spell'/'Item' word (shop, and hand when it holds two cards or fewer)
items.shows: What the spell does and that it is a spell
items.why: The arched lilac tile already says 'spell'. The text repeats on every copy, e.g. 'Play for 1 gold. Three combine into a Stash.' on every Acorn.
items.replacement: An arched tile with art and the gold cost knot. Delete the 'Spell'/'Item' word. Name and text go to the reader.

items.element: Tier knot on unit tiles (shop, board, hand, combat, scout)
items.shows: The unit's tier
items.why: A unit's tier never changes and an experienced player knows it. A 52-px disc covers the portrait's corner on all 14 combat tiles, and Battlegrounds shows no tier on minions.
items.replacement: Shown in the reader's knot (card_detail.gd:103-105). The freed top-left corner is used only by a cost knot when a unit's price isn't the standard 3 (poached).

items.element: Cost knot on spells and items
items.shows: Gold cost, or an Acorn's gold value
items.why: Costs differ from spell to spell and get checked against gold on every buy. Battlegrounds shows tavern spell costs too.
items.replacement: None.

items.element: Stat beads (Attack nut, Health rosehip, hurt rosehip)
items.shows: Current Attack and Health, and whether the unit is damaged
items.why: Core state that changes all the time and feeds every decision. It can't be inferred.
items.replacement: None needed. Optional: once chips and knots are gone, board beads can drop from 84 to about 72 px (numbers stay at 36 or more, above the 31 minimum) to show more art.

items.element: Golden marks: gilt glow, gilt face, gold knot, spark star, gilded art frame
items.shows: The unit is golden
items.why: Golden is real state that changes the text and can't be read from the portrait, so it stays. But five marks say the same thing.
items.replacement: Keep the gilded art frame and the soft glow. Cut the spark star; the gold knot goes with the tier knot.

items.element: Gold glow on a Bird that used a Golden Egg ('egged')
items.shows: This Bird can't take another Golden Egg
items.why: It reuses the golden glow on a unit that isn't golden, so it reads wrong. The restriction is rare, and the reader already says 'Golden Egg used' (card_detail.gd:427-428).
items.replacement: No mark on the tile. The reader line stays.

items.element: Created marks: pine face and dashed burned edge
items.shows: The unit was made by a card, not bought
items.why: Created only changes the sell value (0 instead of 1 gold, rulebook 4.3.3), and the Sell button already shows the amount.
items.replacement: The reader's type line says CREATED, and the Sell button shows 0. In fights, the summon scale-in already shows a unit appearing.

items.element: Frost: double rim, rime on the art, frost face, and the 'FROZEN kept next turn' tag on the first offer
items.shows: The shop is frozen
items.why: Frozen is real state; Battlegrounds shows ice on the tavern. 'Kept next turn' explains Freeze, and the button already reads 'Unfreeze'.
items.replacement: Keep the rime over the art and one frost rim. Cut the tag. Animate the change: on Freeze, rime creeps over each offer left to right, 0.25 s each, staggered 0.05 s; on Unfreeze it cracks and falls away.

items.element: Counter slip on tiles ('1/3', 'In 1/1', 'Hex 2 (4 stored)', '2 left', '3 turns', '3g'/'No ammo', 'Bitter 3', 'Kiss 1/3')
items.shows: Countdowns, Belly contents, stored Hex, ammo, Bitter after borrowing, kisses
items.why: This is hidden state a player needs and can't see anywhere else. The words around the number are teaching.
items.replacement: A number-only pip (31 minimum, at most 64 px wide) in the glyph's spot, replacing the glyph like Battlegrounds' Avenge counter: '1/3'; '1/1' with a small belly outline; '2' with a purple curl for Hex; '0' with an acorn for ammo; '3' for Bitter. The breakdowns ('4 stored', '2 base + 1 from beside', 'toward The Prince Restored') stay in the reader. When the count changes, the pip flips (scale-x 1 to 0 to 1, 0.2 s). On reaching its goal, item 1's glyph animation plays.

items.element: Status slips in fights (Shield, 'Mired +1', Nightshade, Waiting, Stalled, Borrowed, First Bite, Shell, Warned)
items.shows: Statuses granted during the fight
items.why: Statuses are granted mid-fight, so they can't be inferred from the card and must stay. But a word slip covers the tile's top edge and shows only one status; '+1' hides the rest.
items.replacement: One visual per status, applied with a short animation and stacking freely. Shield: a translucent bubble that fades in over 0.2 s and bursts into shards (0.25 s) when it stops a hit. Shell: a pale shell rim that cracks when used. Nightshade: the existing berry icon on the Health bead plus a purple tint; on the first attack, half the Health drains with a purple drip (0.3 s). Mired: a mud rim across the tile's foot, splashed on from the Mire unit across (0.35 s). Waiting (Bide): 'z' curls drifting up on a 1.2 s loop. Warned: a whistle-note icon on the Attack bead. First Bite: a fang glint on the Attack bead before its first exchange. Borrowed and Stalled: reader only. The reader already lists each one as 'On this unit: X' (card_detail.gd:429-439).

items.element: Board name strip with slot code ('F1 Annis x2'), recruit
items.shows: The unit's name and its slot code
items.why: A full 44-px strip above the front row and another below the back row, about 100 of the phone's 780 px, labelling units the player placed and slots the tutorial teaches ('Your board is a brick wall'). Battlegrounds shows no names on the board.
items.replacement: Nothing. Names go to the reader, and slot codes F1-B3 stay in the tutorial and in text that names slots. The Ring count moves onto the ring (next item). Same art caveat as shop names: units on the shared tribe portrait need their own art first.

items.element: Ring header badge ('+3/+3 · 2', 'x36') and the dotted ring
items.shows: Ring stats and Ring count on a slot
items.why: The dotted ring is a good picture of slot state. The stats in the badge are already counted in the standing unit's stats and listed in the reader's slot note. The count matters (Ring size times count, and Reel-Mistress moves Rings).
items.replacement: Keep the dots. When there is more than one Ring, show the count as a small number on a toadstool at the ring's top-right. When a Ring appears, its dots pop up around the slot one by one over 0.3 s. When a Ring moves (Reel-Mistress), the dots run along the zigzag grooves to the next unit, 0.08 s per slot.

items.element: 'Pass end' / 'Pass lands' marker (green slip and arrow on a tile)
items.shows: Which unit a Pass will land on
items.why: A permanent sign showing where a rule points (the last unit on the zigzag), drawn over that unit's art. The rule is taught on the 'Follow the zigzag' page.
items.replacement: Cut the permanent mark and the selection preview. When a Pass fires (End of Turn in recruit, or in a fight), a gold mote leaves the giver and hops slot to slot along the zigzag grooves, 0.08 s per hop, skipping gaps. audits.notes:
I read the code on ideation/wave1 (Bramble-ideation-balance), plus the screenshots listed in the brief and the evidence/ui folder. After these changes, a tile shows a portrait, Attack and Health, at most one glyph or counter, and state pictures (golden, frost, statuses, nest, ring). Everything else is one tap away in the reader. Relations and events become animation.

Biggest wins, in order: the trigger/keyword chips, the text/name/tribe on shop tiles, the recruit name strips, the quarry lines, and the fight's automatic keyword note.

Two things block the cuts:
1. **Missing art.** 50 of 157 unit files have no portrait of their own and fall back to a shared tribe portrait (ui_theme.gd:210-228). Names can't leave the shop or board tiles until those units have art. Done means 5 needs that art anyway.
2. **No recruit animation.** The recruit phase animates almost nothing: only _pulse_new_hand_card (recruit_actions.gd:70). End turn jumps straight to the fight (recruit_screen.gd:984-991), so End of Turn, Pass and Ring effects already happen unseen. Build the glyph animation (item 1) and the Pass mote before removing the chips and the Pass marker. Otherwise the player loses the information instead of seeing it move.

Follow-on changes:
- docs/ideation/wording-guide.md says card text is 'Always shown' on the card face and that on-card tags use the same words; both need rewriting to 'tiles show glyphs, text lives in the reader'.
- The card_view.gd header comment needs the same change.
- Tests that read chip_shown or rules_shown, and roster tests that reject the generic 'Ability' tag, will need rewriting.
- Removing words from tiles also ends most phone-minimum layout fights. Glyphs and pips should be at least 44 px.

These overlap other areas, so I mention them rather than judge them:
- Attack yarn, the ATTACKING/TARGET tags and attacker/defender outlines.
- The combat log and hit panel; the slot chips F1-B3 in fights, which the log refers to.
- Reed links and the pack bracket in lane_overlay.
- Empty-slot notes ('behind F1 & F2'), 'Board 7/7', and the 'Ring size' and 'Tribe bonus' headers.

The 'Not built' chip is dev-only and should never reach a playtest build.

All animation timings assume speed x1; they scale with the existing speed setting and fall back to flash-only under reduce motion.

items.element: THIS HIT panel (purple box, top left): attacker → target name chips, before / hit / after rosehips with numbered discs
items.where: Combat, left column top. src/ui/widgets/hit_panel.gd (whole file); built at combat_screen.gd:108-109, laid out at :288-289, fed by :580-582 begin, :702 add_hit, :734 add_death
items.shows: Who is attacking whom, the target's Health before the hit, the damage, the Health after, and 'dies'
items.why: Everything in it is already on the board: the attacker moves, the damage pops on the target, its Health bead changes, the tile falls. An experienced player watches the tiles, not a sum in a side panel. Battlegrounds has nothing like it. On phone it takes 692 of 2337 canvas px of width and 348 px of height. The look was chosen partly because 'its this hit panel explains a fight best' (DECISIONS.md:823), which was a critic scoring a still screenshot.
items.replacement: Nothing takes the panel's place. The full lunge (attack yarn item) shows who hits whom. The damage pop and the Health bead rolling to its new value show before, hit and after. The death hold shows 'dies'. The freed left column holds the two hero plaques.

items.why: This step is real: if Health just jumps from 26 to 12 the player can't see why. But it is an event, and the text chip restates the rule.
items.replacement: At contact, before the damage pop: a purple Nightshade berry (48 px) drops onto the defender's Health bead (0.15 s, ease-in). The bead flashes Nightshade purple and its number rolls from the old value to half (26 → 13, 0.25 s). Then the normal damage pop and roll (13 → 12). The Nightshade tag on the source pulses 1→1.3→1 as the berry falls, so the source is seen. The keyword sound stays. The health_loss hold stays 0.65 s at ×1.

items.replacement: Counter-damage pops on the attacker's Health bead on the same contact frame as the defender's. Bristle: three short thorns jut from the defender's edge toward the attacker (0.12 s) just before the attacker's damage pop, so it looks different from a plain counter-hit.

It still helps with the rare 'what just happened?', and reviewers use it, so it moves one tap away rather than being deleted.

It disappears on mouse-out, and playback continues. Phone: a tap opens the same reader and pauses playback; tapping anywhere closes it and resumes. The reader also gains the fight-only state cut from the board: whose quarry it is, its Mire binding, the Hex amount on its slot, how many units are inside it, kisses so far, and why it skipped. 'Tap any unit to read it' goes on how-to-play's first page.

items.element: ATTACKING slip
items.shows: Labels the attacking tile
items.why: The tile that leaves its pocket and hits is the attacker. The slip covers that tile's name and art (combat_mid screenshots: it sits on the 'Ring' unit).
items.replacement: The full lunge (attack yarn item).

items.element: TARGET slip ('TARGET Nan Toadstool')
items.shows: Names the defender
items.why: The lunge landing on the defender shows it. At phone size the slip covers a neighbour's stats and is itself crossed by quarry lines ('TARGE` Nan Toadstool' in combat_mid_1688x780.jpg).
items.replacement: The full lunge landing on the target (attack yarn item).

items.element: Attack yarn: red-stitched line with an arrowhead, routed around tiles (back-row attacks loop outside the tray), left up until the next attack
items.shows: Who attacks whom, as a static line
items.why: The owner names targeting arrows as exactly the static images to remove. A line was needed only because the current lunge moves 22% of the way (combat_screen.gd:604 lerp 0.22) and barely leaves the pocket. A real lunge makes the line redundant.
items.replacement: A full lunge on every attack, through _tween so speed scales. (1) Lift, 0.10 s: the attacker's z-index goes above everything, scale 1.0→1.1, drop shadow 6→18 px. (2) Travel, 0.16 s ease-in quad, in a straight line until the attacker's leading edge overlaps the target by about 15% of tile height. A back-row attacker flies over its own front row, and the lift makes this read as a leap. (3) Contact: a 0.05 s hit-stop with both tiles frozen, then both shake (existing _shake), both damage pops play, and the hit sound sized by damage (exists). (4) Return, 0.20 s ease-out to its pocket, scale back to 1.0. About 0.5 s at ×1, replacing the separate 0.5 s attack and 0.5 s damage holds. Pack: the joiners lift 0.04 s after the leader and land on the same target 0.03 s apart; only the leader gets a counter-damage pop, so the rule is shown, not written. Pounce and Counter: no lift, a 0.12 s snap travel and a distinct sound. The yarn stays only under Settings.reduce_motion: drawn straight for 0.4 s, then gone.

items.element: Attacker, defender and joiner outlines held through the attack
items.shows: Highlights the attacker (acorn) and target (red) until the next attack
items.why: They repeat the lunge and leave coloured frames on the board while other events play.
items.replacement: No held outlines. Short colour flashes (0.25 s or less) remain only inside trigger and status animations.

items.element: Damage burst: a 150 px red star with '−N', placed at the card's right edge
items.shows: The damage each unit takes
items.why: Damage numbers are how Battlegrounds shows hits, and an experienced player reads them at a glance. But the star is centred 38% of a tile's width right of centre, so it covers the neighbouring tile (combat_mid_1920x1080.jpg: the −5 covers the F1/F2 boundary).
items.replacement: Keep the outlined −N. Centre it on the struck unit's Health bead, with the star about 96 canvas px and the number at least 52 px. Scale 0.4→1.15→1.0 in 0.12 s, hold 0.25 s, drift up 16 px and fade over 0.15 s. The star size steps up with the existing sound tiers (up to 2, up to 6, more). At the same moment the bead rolls to its new value and flashes red for 0.15 s. When a Shield blocks the hit there is no number; the bubble shatters instead.

items.element: Hit shake
items.shows: That a tile was struck
items.why: It is feel and takes no space.
items.replacement: None.

items.element: Death: the tile tilts, falls 44 px and fades, with a puff of six leaves
items.shows: That a unit died
items.why: This is the woodland version of Battlegrounds' shatter, and it is the 'why it died' moment, but only if the cause is seen first.
items.replacement: Add a timing rule so the cause reads. A unit at 0 Health holds for 0.15 s after whatever brought it there (damage pop, halving roll, thorns, effect mote), then tilts and falls. Units that die in the same event fall together. A 'when this dies' unit's trigger mark pulses as it falls, and its effect launches from where it fell. Swallowed units don't fall (see the event chips item).

items.shows: Who you are fighting and their hero Health

Each of the winner's starting survivors pulses and flicks a spark to the loser's plaque (0.08 s apart), plus a larger spark from the winner's plaque for the round base. The loser's plaque shakes, a −N pop lands on its rosehip, and the number rolls down. A tie with a toll: one spark from the gap between the trays to each plaque. items.replacement: Moves into the single control row.

items.shows: Advances the fight one event

items.shows: That a side has no unit able to attack

items.element: 'Mousewife: no room for a Mouse' caption
items.shows: That a summon failed for lack of room
items.why: A sentence for an event the player can see happen.
items.replacement: A Mouse tile at 40% scale pops out of the source, bumps the full tray's edge and bursts into a grey puff (0.3 s). Once per fight, as now.

items.replacement: The source hops (up 10 px and back, 0.18 s), and its trigger mark on the card face (keyword chip or icon, owned by the card-face review) scales 1→1.5→1 with a 0.25 s acorn glow. The keyword sound plays (exists). Then one 24 px mote in the tribe's colour flies from the source to each affected unit on a slight arc (0.22 s, 0.05 s apart). On arrival the target's change plays: stat pop, status visual or damage pop. Whole-board effects send one ripple from the source across the targets instead of motes. Start of Combat effects play one source at a time in reading order, so the order is visible.

items.replacement: The status's own visual on the tile (shield bubble, berry tag and so on) scales in from 0.3 to 1.0 with a 0.25 s flash in UiTheme.status_colour. When a Shield blocks a hit, the bubble shatters into shards (0.2 s).

items.element: Quarry links: gold dashed diagonal lines from each hunter to its quarry, paw marks, and the 'Marked' chip
items.where: lane_overlay.gd:35-59 (links and paws), redrawn every frame from LaneProjection.playback (lane_projection.gd:127-158); combat_lanes_view.gd:34 'Marked' chip
items.shows: Which enemy each hunter is locked onto, for the whole fight
items.why: These are the 'diagonals on the board' the owner named: up to six crossing lines over the tiles' art and stats for the whole fight (rival-fight, combat_mid screenshots). Nobody makes a decision during a fight, and each time the hunter lunges at its quarry the link is shown at the moment it matters.
items.replacement: At the bell each hunter shoots a gold thread to its quarry (0.25 s), a paw stamp thumps onto the quarry tile's top corner (scale 1.6→1, 0.15 s), and the thread snaps back (0.15 s). The small paw (about 32 px) stays on the quarry as a status mark, as Battlegrounds shows keywords. The lines never stay. Which hunter it is shows in either unit's reader. Take and Poach: when the quarry falls, a coin flies from it to the hunter side's hero plaque (0.35 s, coin sound) instead of the 'Take!' and 'Poach claim' chips.

items.element: Mire: green dashed reed links, mud strips under pockets with the word 'MIRE', and the 'Mire' and 'Mire: waits' chips
items.shows: Which enemy slot each mirer has bogged, and that a mirer waits once
items.why: The patch is real state: the enemy standing there must attack the maker. The link line and the word are reminders of who and what.
items.replacement: At the bell a mud splash travels from the maker straight across to the enemy pocket (0.3 s) and spreads into a patch under it, with two reeds sprouting (0.15 s). The patch stays as texture only, with no word and no link line. Mire waits: when the maker's turn comes it lifts as if to attack, then sinks back as a bog bubble pops (0.3 s), and the next attacker goes. The forced attack shows as the mired enemy's lunge at the maker.

items.element: Pack bracket (gold bracket over the pack's tiles) and the 'Pack!' chip
items.shows: Which units joined a pack attack
items.why: A static bracket and a word for something the attack itself can show.
items.replacement: The joiners' lunge described in the attack yarn item: they lift 0.04 s after the leader and land on the same target, and only the leader takes counter-damage.

items.element: Other event word chips: 'Pounce!', 'Counter!', 'Gulp!', 'Pinched!', 'Whistle!', 'Cancelled', 'Skips: reason', 'Hex!', 'A prince!'
items.shows: That a specific event just happened
items.why: Each is a caption for an event that can be shown as motion.
items.replacement: Each becomes motion, no words. Pounce/Counter: the snap lunge (attack yarn item). Gulp: the swallowed tile shrinks into the swallower's centre (0.25 s), the swallower bulges 1.15→1 (0.15 s), and its held count ticks up. Pinched: the ability chip peels off the victim's face and flies to the taker (0.3 s). Whistle: a ring expands from the whistler across the warned units (0.35 s), which flash in the warned colour. Cancelled: the trigger's mote reaches its target and fizzles into grey smoke (0.2 s). Skip: the unit lifts 6 px and sinks back with a small head-shake (±0.05 rad, 0.25 s); the reason goes to the reader and the log. Hex: a purple sigil spins onto the enemy slot (0.3 s) and the occupant's Attack bead rolls down in red. Transform: the tile flips edge-on and back (scaleX 1→0→1, 0.4 s) to show the prince.

items.element: Kiss counter chip ('Kiss 2/3')
items.shows: Progress toward the transform, a countdown not visible anywhere else in the fight
items.why: This is hidden countdown state, so it must stay visible. It should be a lasting pip, not a floating phrase that vanishes.
items.replacement: Three small pips on the unit's face (card-face area), and 'Kisses: 2 of 3' in its reader. On each kiss a heart flies from the dying mired enemy to the unit (0.3 s) and a pip fills. At 3, the transform flip plays.

items.element: Arrival words ('Summoned', 'Out!', 'Home!', 'Split!')
items.shows: A unit arrived, and how
items.why: Where the unit comes from already says how it arrived.
items.replacement: Each arrival starts from its source. A death summon grows out of where its source fell (0.3→1, back ease, 0.3 s, exists). 'Out!' slides from the holder's tile into its pocket (0.3 s). 'Home!' drops in from above the tray edge (0.35 s). 'Split!' slides sideways out of its parent. A 0.2 s moss outline flash, no word.

items.element: Fight slot marks: the Hex slip ('Hex −4') and the slot trap ('Marked: 3' chip and red-highlighted pocket)
items.where: combat_screen.gd:500-503, :800-812 _slot_mark/_mark_slot; combat_lanes_view.gd:95-100 show_hex; slot_marks.gd hex slip
items.shows: Modifiers that stay on a slot for the rest of the fight and hit whoever stands there or enters
items.why: This is real hidden state that bites later, for example a summon into a trapped slot, so it stays. The text slip and the whole-pocket highlight are louder than it needs.
items.replacement: Hex: a small purple sigil (about 36 px) in the pocket's corner; the amount shows in the reader of the unit standing there. Trap: a small red stake glyph in the pocket's corner, with its damage number at FONT_SMALL, since that number is shown nowhere else. When a unit enters, the stake springs up and the damage pop plays.

items.element: Result panel: dark overlay and 1000×660 plaque with Victory/Defeat, 'X dealt N damage to you', the cap note, toll note, Spoils, rules notes, Watch again and Continue
items.shows: The outcome, the damage, and why the damage is that amount
items.why: The outcome and damage are now animated onto the hero plaques. '(N before the cap)', the toll and the Last Blow notes explain rules.
items.replacement: A banner across the gap between the trays: 'Victory', 'Defeat' or 'Tie' at FONT_TITLE with '−N' beside it, and leaves for Watch again, Continue and Log. The boards are not dimmed. The cap, toll and Last Blow notes go to the log page. The damage rules stay in how-to-play 'Stay standing to win'.

audits.notes:
I judged the fullest UI, /home/alex/code/Bramble-ideation-balance on ideation/wave1, from its code and screenshots, without running Godot. File:line references point into that tree.

1. What the screen becomes. On phone (1688x780, which is 2337x1080 canvas, the 'wide' layout) the left column is 692 px and the right is 489 px. Together they take about half the width. After these calls, the screen holds the two trays, two small hero plaques beside them, and one control row at the bottom right (pause, speed, Skip; step only while paused). The yarn and TARGET slip lived in the 72 px TRAY_GAP. That gap can drop to about 32 px and the trays can grow a little. The boards are limited by height, so the main gain is focus, not much bigger tiles.

2. What the animations have to carry (Done means 5: 'who hits, what triggered, why it died'):
   - Who hits: the full lunge (lift, travel, hit-stop, return).
   - What triggered: the source hops and its trigger mark pulses, then a mote flies to each target.
   - Why it died: a 0.15 s hold at 0 Health after a visible cause (damage pop, halving roll, thorns, mote, swallow), then the fall.
   - The existing sounds (combat_sounds.gd) already map attack, hit size, keyword, death and summon, and they do much of this work. Keep them.
   - The yarn survives only as the reduce-motion fallback.

3. Hidden state that leaves the board, and where it goes:
   - Moves to the one-tap reader: quarry relation, Mire binding, Hex amount, held count, kisses, skip reason.
   - Stays on the board, small and wordless: quarry paw, mud patch, hex sigil, trap glyph with its number, kiss pips.
   - Moves to an opt-in page from the pause menu and the result banner: the whole log.
   - Combat is pure watching: no decision is made during a fight, so none of the cuts takes away a decision input. Scouting and recruit previews of quarry and Mire are other areas.

4. Things that depend on other areas:
   - The trigger mark that pulses, the status visuals, the kiss pips and the held badge are all on the card face (card_view.gd), the card-face reviewer's area.
   - The dotted grooves between the rows (board_view.gd:330-347) are also diagonals on the fight board, drawn unlit and showing nothing a watcher needs. I'd hide them in combat, but they belong to the board area.
   - The empty-pocket words and slot chips are shared with recruit (slot_view.gd, board_view.gd). My calls apply to combat only.

5. How it gets reviewed. The critics scored still screenshots. A still frame rewards labels, lines and panels and can't see animation at all, which is how this clutter won. Fight readability now has to be judged from motion: short recordings or frame strips (for example 8 frames per attack at phone size) from the scripted UI driver, not single screenshots. The look was picked partly for 'its this hit panel explains a fight best' (DECISIONS.md:823). That reason is now overruled by the owner's 9 Nov direction and should be logged as such.

6. Keep the code paths tests rely on: CombatLog describe and LogNote.all_text, and the AttackYarn route for reduce-motion. Only remove their on-screen presentation.

audits.area: Recruit-phase panels and HUD (economy column, hand tray, Birds away tray, Ring/tribe chips, hero plaque, Scout/Who? tokens, Board counter, toasts)

items.element: Birds away tray (paper panel under the hand: 'Birds away', 'Now → landing', 'One Swallow · home in 1 turn', '7/8 → 14/16 · F3', doorstep lines)
items.where: Recruit. src/ui/widgets/away_tray.gd:102-106 (show_state adds 'Now → landing'), src/ui/screens/recruit_held.gd:203-233 (sky_card), placed by src/ui/screens/recruit_layout.gd:256-284 (_layout_hand, which also shrinks the hand to 130-px minis and hides the Board chip)
items.shows: Which Birds are off the board, turns until each comes home, current and homecoming stats, Nest slot, Birds waiting for hand room
items.why: Who is away and when they come back is hidden state. A Nest covered by a recruit or replaced by a newer Nest shows no Egg, so the board can't show it. Everything else is teaching or arithmetic. The heading and the 'Now → landing' legend explain the panel. The stat arrows apply a fixed rule: homecoming doubles base plus permanent stats (rulebook 12.1.4). The slot names repeat the Egg tile, which already reads 'home in 2'. The whole panel is a paper sheet of 31-px text, and it squeezes the hand.
items.replacement: One round bird token per Bird away, 104 canvas px (122 on phone), in a row along the bottom of the hand tray. Each token has the bird's portrait and a small moon badge with the turns left as a digit, and no words. A Bird on the doorstep sits on the tray rim with a closed-door mark instead of the digit. Tapping a token opens the reader (now and home stats, Nest slot), and its Nest slot glows while the reader is open. Animations: (a) Fly South: the sold card lifts off, shrinks into its token and arcs into the row (0.5 s, wing-flap sound), and an Egg drops into the Nest with a bounce (0.25 s). (b) Start of Turn: each moon digit flips down one with a flap (0.2 s, staggered 0.08 s). (c) Homecoming: the token swoops into the hand and unfolds into its card while Attack and Health count up from the old values to the doubled ones (0.6 s), and its Egg cracks and vanishes (0.3 s). (d) When the hand has room, a doorstep token hops in (0.3 s). The hand keeps its normal size.

items.element: Tier up / Refresh / Freeze leaves (word + icon + cost pill, 442×128 each)
items.shows: The three shop actions, their gold costs, and whether the shop is frozen
items.why: Every auto-battler player knows upgrade, refresh and freeze, and Battlegrounds shows them as icon buttons with a cost. The words only help in the first game. The costs and the frozen state change and must stay: Tier up gets cheaper each turn and with A Leg Up. The column takes about a fifth of the phone width and forces narrow shop tiles.
items.replacement: Keep the leaf shapes and colours and drop the words: icon plus cost pill (tier stack + cost, circular arrows + cost, snowflake). Height comes down to the phone tap size (122 canvas px) and the column narrows from 442 to about 300, giving roughly 140 px to the shop and board. While frozen, the snowflake leaf stays pressed in with a darker frost fill. The word appears on long-press or hover. Refreshing gets a sweep: the shelf cards flip away left to right and new ones flip in (0.35 s total).

items.element: End turn second line ('0 + starting survivors'; in other modes 'then fight Old Tansy' or 'Toll 3, cap 5')
items.shows: The damage formula for this fight (round base + 1 per enemy starting survivor), or who you fight next
items.why: It is a rules reminder printed on the most-pressed button. The formula is already on how-to-play's 'Stay standing to win' page, and Battlegrounds never shows its damage formula or cap. The base follows a fixed schedule (game_config.gd:25), learned the way BG players learn tier-based damage. The opponent's name repeats the lobby strip's red 'Next:' plaque.
items.replacement: Remove the line; how-to-play keeps the formula. Make damage felt at the end of each fight on the combat screen: the round's base lands first as one big spark on the loser's lobby plaque, then each of the winner's surviving starting units flicks one small spark to it, 0.12 s apart, with the Health ticking down per spark. Units summoned during the fight send nothing, which teaches 'starting survivors' without words.

items.element: End turn leaf size (189 px tall, 61-px label)
items.shows: Ends recruiting and starts the fight
items.why: Needed, and it is the one button that can't be undone, so it keeps its word. With the sub-line gone it doesn't need the extra height.
items.replacement: Keep 'End turn' on the moss leaf, about 140 px tall and at the narrower column width. When pressed, the leaf curls away (0.25 s) as the screen moves to combat.

items.element: Gold plaque acorn pile and the word 'GOLD'
items.shows: Gold again, as one acorn per coin up to 10, plus a label
items.why: Both repeat the big number. Unspent gold carries over (how-to-play page 2), so above 10 the pile is wrong. The big acorn already says it is gold.
items.replacement: Nothing; the plaque shrinks to the big acorn and the number (about 260×100 instead of 430×152). Spending becomes motion: on a buy, one acorn per gold of cost flies from the plaque to the card (0.3 s) while the number ticks down; on a sale, acorns fly from the sold card into the plaque.

items.element: Gold number with the big acorn
items.shows: Gold you have now
items.why: Core state for every decision, and nothing else shows it.
items.replacement: Unchanged, inside the smaller plaque. The plaque should also stay visible while the reader is open on phone; today recruit_layout.gd:330-335 hides it when a shop card is selected, just when you are deciding whether to buy.

items.element: 'Next +5' income line on the gold plaque
items.shows: Next turn's scheduled income; the tooltip adds queued gold, Spoils and debt
items.why: The schedule is fixed and taught (3 gold, then +1 a turn up to 10, as in BG), so on a normal turn it is a reminder. Gold queued by cards (Rainy Day, Jack Daw, a Shy walk-out's +2) and debt repayment are hidden state that nothing else shows.
items.replacement: Show nothing when next income matches the schedule. When gold is queued or debt is being repaid, show a small ghost-acorn badge on the plaque corner with only the difference ('+2' in gold, '−1' in red); tap it for the full income line in the reader. When a card queues gold, its acorns drop into the badge (0.3 s). At Start of Turn the badge's acorns pour into the number.

items.element: 'Tier 4' label with tier icon (its own row)
items.shows: Your current shop tier
items.why: Needed and not visible elsewhere, but it doesn't need a word and a row. Battlegrounds puts the tier as a badge on Bob next to the upgrade button.
items.replacement: A digit inside the Tier up leaf's tier-stack icon, so the icon is the current-tier badge and the leaf adds the cost pill. At top tier the leaf greys and shows only the badge. On tier up the digit flips up and the stack gains a step (0.4 s) while the new shop deals in.

items.element: 'Turn 2' label
items.shows: Round number
items.why: It sets the round's base damage and the Spoils rounds, and after turn 8 gold no longer gives it away, so experienced players still glance at it. It doesn't need its own row in the economy column.
items.replacement: A small 'Turn 8' (31 px, the phone minimum) inside the gold plaque, where 'GOLD' was.

items.element: Hand tray title 'Hand'
items.shows: Names the tray
items.why: The cards in it and where it sits say what it is; a label only helps the first game.
items.replacement: Plain oak tray. A buy teaches it by motion: the bought card lifts off the shelf and flies into the tray (0.35 s).

items.element: Hand count '1/10'
items.shows: Cards in hand against the limit of 10
items.why: The limit only matters when you hit it (Birds wait on the doorstep, a Triple goes to the board). Below that, the cards and the '+N more' button show the count.
items.replacement: Hidden below the limit. At 10/10 a small red '10/10' appears on the tray corner. When a full hand blocks a buy, the tray rim flashes red and the card snaps back to the shelf (0.3 s).

items.element: Empty-hand hint 'Bought units wait here. Drag one to an empty slot.'
items.shows: How buying and playing works
items.why: Pure teaching that shows every time the hand is empty, which is most of a game. How-to-play page 1 already says 'Buy a unit for 3 gold and drag it to an empty slot.'
items.replacement: Empty tray. The buy flight (shelf to tray, 0.35 s) and the board's slot glow while dragging show the same thing by motion.

items.element: Instruction lines in the reader while something is selected: 'Tap an empty slot to play it', 'Tap a slot to play it, or an Ooze to swallow it', 'Tap where to play it', 'Tap where to use it', 'Tap a slot to move or swap.', 'Or tap an Ooze to buy it in'
items.shows: How to finish the action you started
items.why: The target glow (recruit_layout.gd:385-427) already lights every legal slot, Ooze and shop card, and tap-or-drag is universal. These lines teach on every selection.
items.replacement: Keep the glow and make it breathe (alpha 0.6 to 1, 0.8 s loop) so it reads as 'here'. The no-target reasons (no_target_note, e.g. 'Every Ring is full', 'Needs a unit in your back row') become feedback: tapping a card with no legal target shakes it (0.25 s) and shows the reason for 2 s.

items.element: 'Board 6/7' chip under the hand
items.shows: Units on board against 7 slots
items.why: The board shows its seven slots, and an empty slot is plain to see. BG has no board counter.
items.replacement: None. If a play is blocked because the board is full, the board tray gives a short shake (0.25 s).

items.element: 'Ring size 1.25' chip above the shop
items.shows: The permanent Ring multiplier (each Ring gives +size/+size)
items.why: Hidden player-level state that changes the value of every Ring, like BG's Blood Gem counter, so it stays. The words 'Ring size' don't need to, and on phone the chip sits on the shop's tier badges.
items.replacement: A ring icon with '×1.25' (31 px) in a small counter column beside the hero portrait; tapping it opens 'Each Ring gives +1.25/+1.25.' in the reader. When the size grows, the counter pulses and every Ring on the board shimmers once (0.4 s). It shows under the same conditions as now.

items.element: 'Midsummer N' chip
items.shows: End of Turns left until Ring size grows (shared clock)
items.why: A countdown nothing else shows, so the number stays and the word goes.
items.replacement: A sun icon with the digit, in the same counter column. Each End of Turn the digit ticks down. At 0 a sun arc sweeps across the board and the Rings flare (0.6 s) while the Ring size counter steps up.

items.element: Tribe bonus caption and chips ('Tribe bonus' + tribe portrait '+1/+1')
items.shows: Earned bonus per tribe, which also applies to units you get later
items.why: Hidden state for future units, like BG's tribe counters, so the chips stay. The caption is a label.
items.replacement: Drop 'Tribe bonus'. Move the portrait-plus-number chips into the counter column by the hero. When a bonus grows, a +1/+1 spark leaps from the chip to each unit of that tribe on the board (0.4 s).

items.element: Hero plaque name ('Brother Bracken')
items.shows: Your hero's name
items.why: You chose the hero, and the portrait identifies it. On phone the name takes two lines and needs ellipses. Tapping the portrait still opens the hero card with the name.
items.replacement: None; the portrait fills the plaque.

items.element: Hero portrait
items.shows: Who you are; tapping opens the hero card
items.why: It is identity and the way to read your power. Armor is hidden state that matters for decisions, but today it only appears in the tapped text ('Armor N: lost before Health').
items.replacement: Unchanged, plus a small grey shield with the armor number on its corner when armor is above 0, as BG does. When armor absorbs damage after a fight, the shield chips and the number ticks down.

items.element: Hero power leaf 'Power' with cost badge
items.shows: The usable hero power, its cost and whether it is spent
items.why: The cost and the spent or unaffordable state are needed. The word 'Power' is a label.
items.replacement: A round button under the portrait showing the power's icon and the cost badge, greyed when spent or unaffordable. On use it flips to its back (0.3 s), as in BG. Pipkin-style limits show as pips on its rim that empty as they are used.

items.element: Scout token (and its 'Close' state)
items.shows: Opens and closes the next opponent's last board
items.why: It does the same as tapping the red 'Next:' plaque in the lobby strip, which already opens scouting (lobby_strip.gd:44-45). BG players scout from the leaderboard portrait.
items.replacement: Tap the Next plaque to open; it stays lit while open, and tapping it again or the table closes it. Their board slides down out of the plaque into the shop's place (0.3 s) and back up on close, so where it comes from is felt. How-to-play's 'Scout who you fight next' changes 'Tap Scout' to 'Tap your next opponent at the top'.

items.element: Who? token (shown while scouting)
items.where: Recruit, left margin. src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd:174-177, 260-266; src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd:178-198 (ghost_card, opponent_card)
items.shows: Their hero card, or what a ghost is
items.why: A second button for something the scout heading can do. The ghost card's 'It has no Health; if it wins, you still lose Health' is a rule.
items.replacement: The scout panel heading becomes their hero portrait plus name; tapping it opens their hero card in the reader. The ghost rule moves to how-to-play.

items.element: Scout heading 'Rival 4 · Brother Bracken's last fight'
items.shows: Whose board this is, and that it is their last one
items.why: Whose board it is matters. 'last fight' explains what scouting shows, which experienced players know.
items.replacement: Their portrait and name only (tappable, as above). A ghost shows the Ghost portrait treatment the lobby plaque already uses.

items.element: Ask for Kin leaf (fourth leaf when enabled)
items.shows: A 2-gold, once-a-turn tribe refresh; when it shows, the other leaves shrink
items.why: An action with a cost and a used-this-turn state, so the button stays. Its name and rules are teaching.
items.replacement: Icon only (refresh arrows with a two-portrait mark) plus a '2' cost pill, the same size as the other icon leaves; it greys after use. The rule text stays on long-press (its tooltip exists). Pressing it plays the refresh sweep, and offers sharing your tribes land with a brief tribe-colour glint (0.3 s).

items.element: Shy confirm: End turn, a play or a move that would make a Shy unit leave needs a second press after a warning toast
items.shows: That this action will make a Shy unit walk out
items.why: A confirm-and-warn step re-teaches the Shy rule every time and adds a press for players who meant it. The preview it runs is useful, but it can be shown before the press instead of after it.
items.replacement: While the current board would make a Shy unit leave at End of Turn, that unit plays a small looping fidget: glances toward the board edge and sways 4 px (1.2 s loop). While a dragged card hovers a slot that would trigger it, the fidget starts on the Shy unit right away. End turn and plays take one press. When it does leave, it walks off the board edge (0.4 s) and its gold drops into the gold plaque's next-turn badge.

items.element: Top toasts: 'Next fight: a ghost. Scout it to see.', 'Triple! Golden X in hand: play it for your reward.', 'Triple Reward: X is in your hand.', 'Three Acorns made a Stash.', 'Poached X from your last opponent.', 'A frog gets a kiss (2/3).', 'X walked out of F3 (Shy): +2 gold next turn.', 'New Nest replaces X's at F3…', 'Pipkin's two unit buys are used.', and rejection reasons
items.where: Recruit, over the lobby strip. src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd:29, 905-958 (_after_change, _note_golden_on_board), 960-964; src/ui/screens/recruit_view.gd:501-546 (event_note, change_notices); src/ui/screens/recruit_layout.gd:178
items.shows: Events that just happened and why an action failed
items.why: Each one narrates an event in words. Players read events from motion, and a 3.5 s banner covers the lobby strip.
items.replacement: Ghost-next: cut, since the plaque already reads 'Ghost of X'. Triple: the copies fly together, merge in a gilt flash and the golden card drops into the hand (0.6 s, triple sound); it keeps a slow gilt shimmer until played. Triple Reward: the picked card flies from the picker into the hand (0.35 s). Stash: three acorns slide together and pop into the Stash (0.4 s; extends the pulse in recruit_actions.gd:70-78). Poached: the card flies from that rival's lobby plaque into your shop (0.5 s). Kiss: a heart pops off the frog and one kiss pip fills. Shy walk-out: as in the Shy item. Nest replaced: the old Egg rolls off and the new Nest drops, while the old bird's token stays in the sky row. Pipkin: the power's buy pips empty. Rejections: whatever is short shakes (the gold plaque for gold, the hand rim for a full hand, the board for no room, 0.25 s) with a dull click. Text stays only for rare reasons motion can't show, such as 'Discover found no eligible cards'.

items.element: '+N more' hand button
items.shows: Hand cards past the sixth
items.why: It is the only way to reach overflow cards.
items.replacement: Unchanged.

items.element: Gear (menu) token
items.shows: Pause, settings and quit
items.why: Needed and icon-only already. With Scout and Who? gone it is the only token in the left margin.
items.replacement: Unchanged; the left margin can narrow.

audits.notes:
Code read: /home/alex/code/Bramble-ideation-balance on ideation/wave1 (recruit_screen/layout/view/held/actions, gold_plaque, hero_plaque, away_tray, tribe_bonuses, leaf_button, lobby_strip, how_to_play). The tribes2 strong-field screenshots show the same elements; that branch has no away_tray.gd.

What the cuts add up to: the economy column narrows from 442 to about 300 canvas px. Gold shrinks to the acorn and the number, and the tier sits on the Tier up leaf. Scout and Who? leave the left margin. Board 6/7 goes, and so do the hand's title, count and hint. The Birds away panel becomes a row of portrait tokens. Ring size, Midsummer and tribe bonuses gather as small icon counters beside the hero. On phone that is roughly 140-200 px of width back for the shop and board, and the hand tray stops shrinking whenever birds are away.

What stays because it can't be seen otherwise: gold, tier, turn, costs, frozen state, Birds away and their countdowns, doorstep birds, Ring size, Midsummer, tribe bonuses, queued gold and debt (only when they differ from the schedule), the hero power's cost and spent state, and a full hand.

Hidden state I recommend adding: armor is only shown in the hero card's tap text (recruit_screen.gd:704-711) and should be a shield number on the portrait. Also, on phone the gold plaque and tier leaves hide while the reader is open (recruit_layout.gd:330-335), so you can't see your gold while reading a card you might buy. The narrower column should let them stay.

Almost none of the replacement animations exist yet. The recruit screen's only tween is the Stash pulse (recruit_actions.gd:70-78). The shop-to-hand flight, the acorn flights, the bird token flights and the combat damage sparks are new work. When Settings.reduce_motion is on, motion can't carry the meaning, so those players should get the cut text back as a short toast.

Outside my area but next to it: scouting turns on the lane overlay (recruit_layout.gd:182, lane_overlay.gd), and those dashed forecast lines across the scouted board are the 'diagonals' the owner named. audits.notes:
TUTORIAL GAME SPEC (replaces the 14-page guide that opens before the first game; Done means 5 lists a tutorial). A scripted short game: you plus 3 bots, fixed seed and scripted shops, about 6 rounds, Last Stand off. A coach speaks one line at a time in a speech slip outside the board, and an animated finger performs each new action once. Only the control being taught is lit. The coach exists only inside the tutorial; real games never show it. It can be skipped on first launch and replayed from the menu hub and Settings.
- R1: drag a shop unit to a slot while acorns fly off the gold counter; End turn. The fight runs at x1 and shows the front row taking the hits, lunges and deaths. Afterwards the hero-damage animation plays and the rosehip counts down.
- R2: income rises; sell; refresh; the back row sits behind two front slots. The fight shows sides alternating, the bigger band first.
- R3: tier up (its cost falls each turn); freeze. The red rim means your next opponent: tap it to scout, tap again to close, and tap their portrait to read their hero.
- R4: a scripted triple gives a golden unit and a Discover reward. Then 'press any card to read it'. This step is what makes cutting on-board keyword text safe.
- R5: tribe icons and a tribe bonus; the hero power; buy a spell, play it from the hand onto a target.
- R6: a bot is knocked out (greying animation, grey chip). The next round pairs you with a ghost: 'A ghost: their last board. It has no Health.'
- The end screen points to Rules for Last Stand, Last Blow, Early Spoils, Pass/Shy/Mire, Belly, Fly South/Nest/Egg and Ring.

WHAT THE TUTORIAL MUST COVER SO THE CUTS ARE SAFE (each cut, and where it is taught):
- Next rim = next opponent; tap it to scout and again to close; tap the portrait for their hero. Covers the cuts of 'Next:', the Scout/Close and Who? tokens, the scout title and 'then fight X'. Taught in R3.
- Portrait = hero, rosehip = Health, knot = tier, tap any plaque to read the hero. Covers the cut names and the 'You' word. Taught in R1 and R3.
- Damage = round base + 1 per enemy starting survivor, with a rising base. Covers the cut End turn formula. Taught at the R1 fight end; Rules 'Damage' holds the table; tapping your own plaque gives the current number.
- Elimination grey chip, ghost shimmer, no Health. Covers the cuts of the out-plaque text, 'Ghost of', the NEXT tag, the ghost toast and the Who? ghost card. Taught in R6 and Rules 'Lobby & ghosts'.
- Last Four, Last Stand (gold ring = save unused, crack = used) and Last Blow: rare, so Rules plus the reader on a rosehip, not the tutorial game.
- Front-row targeting, a safe back row, attack order and alternation. Taught in the R1–R2 fights.
- Across = same column; Quarry hunts across; Mire = mud under the slot; press-and-hold shows one unit's links. Covers the cut scout lanes and slot captions. Taught in Rules Keywords demos and the reader.
- The reader (press any card). Taught in R4.
- Gold, refresh, freeze, sell, tier-up discount (R1–R3); triples (R4); tribes, hero power, spells (R5).

DEPENDENCIES AND RISKS:
- Portrait plaques: art exists for all 9 real heroes; only the sample_* test heroes lack it.
- Tier and Health numbers on portrait plaques must stay at or above UiTheme.MIN_FONT on phone.
- State carries only the next opponent's last board. Battlegrounds lets you view any rival's; that is an optional core change, not needed for this audit.
- Overlap with other auditors: the combat 'Fighting' plaque and the end-of-fight damage animation belong to combat; the End turn sub-labels belong to recruit; slot captions and empty-pocket words belong to the board auditor; the paw keyword icon belongs to card_view.
- Reduce motion must keep the fight's information once animation replaces labels (flash in place of lunge).
- Tests that pin current text will need updating: tests/ui/test_polish.gd, test_engines.gd, test_full_game.gd, test_look.gd, test_milestone_b.gd, test_cards.gd, layout_check.gd, shots/playthrough.gd, tests/core/test_full_games.gd. They grep for 'Next: ', 'Last Stand: ', 'Who?', 'last fight', 'Ghost of', 'Changes save' and seen_guide.
- The lobby re-sort by Health is optional; if adopted, log it in DECISIONS.md.

overrules.element: Printed keyword chips for keywords that decide who attacks whom (Mire, Quarry; test Swoop and Bristle the same way)
overrules.from: cut: no static mark, shown only by motion when the keyword acts
overrules.to: shrink: one small wordless mark on the tile frame, the same whether the keyword is printed or granted. Mire gets reeds along the tile foot (Bramble's Taunt frame). A Quarry hunter gets a claw notch on its frame, different from the paw on its prey. Card-specific behaviour (Cleave, Pack, Snap, Peck, Pin, Bide, Whistle) stays motion-only, with its text in the reader.
overrules.why: Battlegrounds keeps the Taunt frame on every Taunt minion even though experts know every card, because that frame is how you read an enemy board at a glance. Here the decision it feeds is positioning against the scouted board: which of their units hunt the slot across, and which force mine to hit them. The scout tray lines up column for column, so a mark on their tile plus the 'across' rule gives the whole read. Recognising 157 units by a 190 px portrait isn't reliable yet: in strong-field lobby_1688x780.png, Brock, Old Brock, Sable and Russet look alike at board size.

overrules.element: Nest countdown digit on the Nest, the 'On Nest' mark under a unit, and the homecoming animation
overrules.from: shrink to a digit badge on the Nest, plus a twig rim under a covering unit; homecoming animates the Bird swooping into its slot
overrules.to: cut from the board. An empty Nest shows the Egg with art and stats, as both audits keep. A covered Nest shows nothing on the board; the covering unit's reader says it stands on a Nest. The countdown appears once, on the Bird's away token (audit 4). Homecoming animates the token flying into the hand, or onto the doorstep when the hand is full.
overrules.why: Rulebook 12.1.4 says the Bird 'enters hand, or waits on the doorstep if hand is full'. It never comes back to the Nest slot. So a digit on the slot counts down to an event that doesn't happen there, and audits 1 and 2 both animate homecoming into the wrong place. The away token already carries the same number, and audit 1's own note 3 asks for one home for it.

overrules.to: shrink (audit 4): a ring icon and '×1.25' in the small counter column by the hero, shown under the same conditions as now
overrules.why: It sets the payoff of every Ring card in the shop, and a Fairy player prices that on every refresh without tapping cards they already know. It can't be worked out from the board's stats.

overrules.element: '+N more' hand button: the hand shows only 5 cards, or 3 while Birds are away
overrules.to: cut the button and show every hand card at once, in one row of minis up to 10, using the width freed by cutting the tray texts and narrowing the right column
overrules.why: The hand is state you decide with every turn: which pairs are close to a triple and what to play next. Hiding cards behind a button takes needed state away. Confirmed in /home/alex/code/Bramble-ideation-balance/src/ui/screens/recruit_screen.gd _render_hand: HAND_SHOWN is 6, and the limit drops to 4 while Birds are away.

overrules.from: reduce-motion players get the cut text back as toasts (audit 4)
overrules.to: flashes in place (audit 5): a brightness flash on the source, then on the target. Numbers still pop, and deaths fade.
overrules.why: Toasts bring back the narration the owner asked to remove, for players who know the game just as well as anyone else.

overrules.to: always sorted by standing and updated after each fight, with the plaques sliding to their new places (0.3 s)
overrules.why: Your standing (top four or not) is the number an expert checks every turn, and Battlegrounds' leaderboard shows it by order alone. Seat order makes you compare eight Health numbers.

overrules.area: Combat and lobby (audits 3, 4 and 5 each give a different version)

overrules.to: all survivors flick their sparks at once, then one thump lands the total. Under 0.6 s at ×1.

Words stay on buttons that act (End turn), in the reader, menus, tutorial and game-over. Critics should judge a still of the resting state by that count, and judge fights from motion strips, not stills (audit 3 note 5). Their persona should be a player in their hundredth game, not a first-timer.

7. Docs to change in the same step: rulebook 12.1.6 (the permanent Pass mark), the wording guide's 'Always shown' and 'selecting lights the slots' lines, and the tests that pin current strings.
