critics.summary:
I mostly agree with the audits. The biggest wins:
- Combat: cut the THIS HIT panel, combat log, keyword box, attack yarn and target slips, and the quarry and Mire lines. A full lunge plus damage pops carries the fight instead.
- Tiles: cut trigger and keyword chips, names, tribe words, tier knots and shop rules text. Text moves to the reader, and triggers become one glyph plus animation.
- Board: cut the name strips, slot codes, empty-slot notes, grooves and the permanent Pass mark.
- HUD: cut the Board count, the hand hints, the damage formula on End turn, and the Scout and Who? tokens.

I overrule ten calls:
- Mire and Quarry keep a small wordless frame mark, like Battlegrounds' Taunt frame. Positioning against a scouted board depends on reading them at a glance, and 157 portraits at 190 px, some alike, won't carry that yet.
- The Nest countdown leaves the board. Birds come home to the hand (rulebook 12.1.4), and audits 1 and 2 animated homecoming into the slot.
- The hand shows all its cards; today it hides cards past the fifth.
- Ring size stays as a small counter.
- The result banner and the Continue tap go; the fight returns to recruit on its own.
- The lobby is always sorted by standing.
- No reach highlight while the reader is open.
- No looping Shy fidget and no Shy confirm.
- Reduce motion uses flashes, not toasts.
- Damage sparks fire at once, not one per survivor.

What the audits missed: before names leave tiles and plaques, every unit needs its own distinct portrait and lobbies need unique heroes. The new animations need a time budget and must never block input. And the critics' method has to change, from scoring stills to counting words at rest and watching motion.

Not run: Godot. All judgements come from the code on ideation/wave1 (/home/alex/code/Bramble-ideation-balance) and the 9 listed screenshots.

overrules.element: Name strip on board tiles ('F1 Annis ×2'), and names on shop tiles
overrules.area: Recruit board (board audit). The card audit already has this caveat.
overrules.to: Cut it on units that have their own portrait. Units still on a shared tribe portrait keep a one-line short name (the 31 minimum) until their art lands.
overrules.why: The chess point only works because every piece looks different. I checked: 50 of 157 units have no assets/portraits/<id>.jpg and fall back to the tribe face, so they can't be learned by sight. Done means 5 needs that art anyway.

overrules.element: Relation highlight (gilt slots a unit's text reaches)
overrules.area: Recruit board (board audit vs card audit)
overrules.from: animate: a 6 px lean during drag only; no highlight on select; cut the 'Highlighted:' line
overrules.to: Keep a slot tint (a) while dragging over a candidate pocket, with the lean, and (b) while that unit's reader is open: one 0.3 s pulse, then a faint tint (the card audit's version). Cut the highlight after the drop and the 'Highlighted:' text.
overrules.why: The wording guide's 'Let the interface carry it' lets card text say beside, behind, next to and touching without explaining them, because selecting a unit lights the slots its text reaches. With slot codes and grooves gone, this tint is the only place those words become concrete. It shows only on demand, not all the time, and it's the same kind of feedback as the legal-target highlight the board audit keeps.

overrules.element: Scout lane forecast (hunter lines, reed links, MIRE patches)
overrules.area: Scout (board audit: cut with nothing; lobby audit: press-and-hold draws links)
overrules.from: cut with nothing / draw one unit's links while held
overrules.to: No lines anywhere. While a unit's reader is open during scouting, the enemy slots it will reach (its across slot, a lent quarry, its Mire patch) take the same tint as in the overrule above.
overrules.why: Quarry isn't always across. A lent quarry points a unit beside the lender at the lender's across slot (lane_projection.gd _mark with own_across false; the log reads 'Sleeping Partner (B2) marks Mrs Sorrel (F3)'). So the lobby audit's 'readable from the lined-up columns' doesn't hold, and cutting the forecast with nothing makes those hunts impossible to learn before the fight. One rule, 'the reader lights what the text reaches', covers both boards and draws no lines.

overrules.element: Slot codes in keyword reminders and Rules text (Behind, Touching, Pass, 'Who attacks when', the scout 'across' line, 'Follow the zigzag')
overrules.area: Reader reminders (keyword_rules.gd, effects.json) and how_to_play.gd. The board audit left this open; the card audit says codes stay in text.
overrules.from: keep F1–B3 in text, or reword (undecided)
overrules.to: Reword without codes. Pass: 'your rightmost unit, other than this, gains X'. Touching: 'a chain of units left to right through both rows; an empty slot breaks it'. Behind: 'each back slot is behind the two front slots it sits between'. Who attacks when: 'front row left to right, then the back row'. Scout: 'straight across'. Only the brick-wall Rules page keeps a labelled diagram.
overrules.why: The zigzag F1-B1-F2-B2-F3-B3-F4 (board_geometry.gd ZIGZAG) is simply left to right across the brick, because the back slots sit at half offsets. So the Pass recipient is just the rightmost unit, which the board already shows. That is what makes cutting the Pass mark, its preview and the grooves safe. Players meet these words in the reader mid-game, where codes would point at labels the board no longer draws.

overrules.element: Full lunge replacing the attack yarn
overrules.from: animate, with every lunge timing run through _tween so ×2 and ×4 scale it
overrules.to: ×2 and ×4 shorten the holds and gaps between events first. The lunge keeps a floor at any speed (travel at least 0.10 s, hit-stop at least 0.04 s). Tutorial fights are locked at ×1.
overrules.why: set_speed applies speed_scale to every tween, so at ×4 the proposed 0.16 s travel takes 0.04 s, about 2 frames. The lunge would no longer show who hits whom, and the yarn that used to show it is gone. Experienced players are the ones who pick ×2 or ×4.

overrules.area: Recruit header (board audit: move to the reader; recruit audit: shrink)
overrules.from: move-to-reader: shown only in the reader of Ring cards, Fairies and ringed slots
overrules.to: The recruit audit's version: a ring icon with '×1.25' in the counter column by the hero. Tapping it opens the reader.
overrules.why: It is hidden state for the whole player, like Battlegrounds' Blood Gem counter. If it lives only in a Ring card's reader, a player finds out the multiplier exists only after holding one.

overrules.element: Last Blow note on the fight result
overrules.from: the cap, toll and Last Blow notes all go to the log page
overrules.to: The cap and toll notes go to the log. When Last Blow decides the fight, the banner shows 'Last Blow' as a linked word next to Victory or Defeat.
overrules.why: When both boards are empty, the fight looks like a tie, and Battlegrounds would call it one. Without the word, the result contradicts what the player just watched, and nothing points to the rule.

overrules.from: 6 scripted rounds, including a tribe-bonus round (R5) and a forced elimination plus ghost round (R6)
overrules.to: 4 rounds, 12 steps (in the summary). Ghosts, eliminations, Last Four, Last Stand and tribe counters are left to the Rules pages and the reader.
overrules.why: Each of those marks can be tapped, and its reader states the rule (ghost_card, the Last Stand line, the tribe chip). The tutorial teaches tapping in step 1. Ghosts work as in Battlegrounds. Scripting an elimination by round 6 adds length without teaching a control.

critics.summary:
Most cuts are safe if two things exist: a short tutorial that teaches tapping a card to read it, and a rule that every mark without words opens the reader when tapped. Eight calls overruled, mostly where the board audit took away the only place a rule shows. The biggest is keeping the reader-open slot tint: the wording guide counts on it so cards needn't explain beside, behind, next to and touching.

Most animations do carry what the static elements showed. Three don't: the lunge at ×4 (about 2 frames), Hunker and Damage Reduction hits (smaller numbers with no visible cause), and Borrowed units.

Smallest tutorial: one scripted game, 4 rounds, about 5 minutes.
- You plus 3 rivals whose boards are fixed for each round (built like content/scenarios), fixed shops, fights at ×1.
- A coach slip sits outside the board. A finger shows each new action once, and only that control works.
- It can be skipped at any time. It replaces the 14-page guide on the first New game, and can be replayed from the menu, Settings and the pause menu.

The steps, in order:
- Round 1:
  (1) Tap a shop unit (hover on PC) to open the reader, then tap its underlined keyword for the reminder.
  (2) Buy it and drag it, or tap a lit slot, into the front row. Acorns fly off the gold.
  (3) End turn. In the fight, which you win: the bell rings, your unit's glyph pulses and its mote flies, then lunges, damage pops and a death. Coach: 'Start of Combat first, then the sides take turns: front row left to right, then the back row.'
- Round 2:
  (4) Sell, refresh (icon leaf; hold it to see its word), buy two, and put one in the back row. Coach: 'The back row is safe until the front row falls.'
  (5) Open a unit with 'beside' text: the slots it reaches glow. Place it. At End of Turn its spark jumps to its neighbours.
  (6) In the fight, which you lose (the rival has the bigger band and goes first): tap a unit, play pauses, the reader opens, tap to go on.
  (7) Damage: the round's base thumps onto your portrait, then one spark for each starting survivor. A summoned survivor sends none. The coach states the rule once.
- Round 3:
  (8) The red rim marks who you fight next. Tap it to see their last board, tap their portrait for their hero, tap the rim again to close.
  (9) Tier up (the cost is lower than last turn), then freeze.
  (10) Skip the fight.
- Round 4:
  (11) A third copy is offered: buy it, the three merge into a golden card in hand, play it and Discover.
  (12) Use the hero power, and play a bought spell onto a unit.
- End: 'The rest is on any card you tap, and in How to play.'

Left to the Rules pages and the reader, not the tutorial: ghosts, eliminations, Last Four, Last Stand, Last Blow, Pass and Touching, Rings, Nests, Belly, Hex, Shy, Mire, Quarry, statuses, counters, tribe and Ring-size counters, the income badge, the hand limit and armor.

- Put 'tap any card, or tap in a fight, to read it' on page 1.
- Reword the slot codes as in the overrule.
- Add 'Start of Combat first' to 'Who attacks when'.
- Change 'Tap Scout' to 'tap your next opponent'.
- Add a page for the lobby, ghosts and the last four.
- Draw the icon-only leaves.
- Turn the static tags into the in-game animations.
